reference: Installed GNU coreutils command-line tools selected by each parity case, executed by the harness reference Bash. Seeded shuffle is only compared on a zero-count/single-item boundary because this loadable documents a different random-source algorithm from GNU.
coverage: Bash type/help metadata contract for the dispatcher
tac with overlapping literal and NUL separators over private binary fixtures
factor multiple operands; fmt paragraph wrapping; tsort on a uniquely ordered chain
nproc OpenMP cap and ignore option with fixed environment values
numfmt IEC conversion in both directions
shuf zero-count and singleton range boundaries
install content, exact modes, and parent directory creation in the private tree
mknod FIFO creation and shred zero-fill/unlink on private relative files
Private FIFO default/explicit modes across umasks, existing-entry preservation, and restored masks after errors.
exclusions: Shuf permutation distribution and seeded output are not GNU byte-parity claims because the documented implementation uses a different random-source algorithm.
Character and block device creation is deferred because the harness removes capabilities and has no device-node mock; physical shred erasure is not established by regular-file fixtures.
The suite does not exercise yes's unbounded output, groups, or every unsupported GNU option.

cases.purpose: Bash metadata must identify coreutils as a builtin and resolve its attached help text without invoking a dispatcher verb.
cases.script: [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]] || exit 1; help coreutils >/dev/null; printf 'metadata ok\n'

cases.purpose: Reverse records using an overlapping multi-byte literal separator and the documented empty-separator NUL mode, preserving binary bytes and unterminated tails.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'A::B:::tail' > overlap; printf 'left\000middle\000last' > nul-records; cu tac --separator='::' overlap; cu tac -s '' nul-records

cases.purpose: Check exact GNU factor formatting across unity, composites and a prime, then verify the malformed-operand error after successful operands.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; cu factor 1 84 360 99991; cu factor not-a-number

cases.purpose: Check word wrapping at a narrow explicit width and preservation of a paragraph boundary.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'alpha beta gamma

zulu
' | cu fmt -w 5

cases.purpose: Check topological ordering where the input graph has one required order, avoiding unspecified tie ordering.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'a b
b c
c d
' | cu tsort

cases.purpose: With fixed OpenMP environment values, verify GNU's thread-limit cap and ignore subtraction without depending on host CPU count.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; export OMP_NUM_THREADS=5 OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=2; cu nproc --ignore=1

cases.purpose: Compare IEC human-readable output and IEC suffix parsing over exact integral values.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf '1024
1536
' | cu numfmt --to=iec; printf '1K
1.5K
' | cu numfmt --from=iec

cases.purpose: Check GNU-compatible zero-output count and singleton integer range boundaries; this deliberately does not assert a random permutation.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'seeddata' > seed; cu shuf --random-source=seed -n 0 -i 1-10; cu shuf --random-source=seed -n 1 -i 7-7

cases.purpose: Verify regular-file replacement copies binary content with an exact requested mode, -D creates relative parent directories, and -d creates a directory with an exact mode.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'blob\000tail\n' > source; printf 'old contents\n' > installed; cu install -m 0640 source installed; cu install -D -m 0751 source nested/deep/copied; cu install -d -m 0700 local/state

cases.purpose: Create a FIFO under a relative private path with an explicit mode and compare its type and exact mode with GNU mknod.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; cu mknod -m 0620 pipe p

cases.purpose: Exercise the explicit zero-fill pass and unlink behavior only on a small generated private fixture; the tree comparison verifies removal.
cases.script: cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; printf 'fixture secret\000bytes\n' > private-file; cu shred -n 0 -z -u private-file

cases.purpose: Cover the loadable's character and block device-node operations when a safe privileged fixture becomes available.
cases.reason: Character/block node creation needs a disposable VM or a reviewed mknod syscall mock with synthetic major/minor numbers. A future case should verify node type, mode, device numbers, existing-path behavior, and the expected permission-denied path. The current capability-free fixture covers FIFO creation only.

cases.purpose: Private FIFO defaults respect umask; explicit modes override it, and later file creation proves the caller mask was restored. No device nodes are created.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; for mask in 000 022 077; do
 (umask "$mask"; cu mknod "pipe-$mask" p; cu mknod -m 0620 "explicit-$mask" p; : > "after-$mask")
done

cases.purpose: Existing and missing-parent FIFO failures preserve the existing node mode and restore umask before subsequent private file creation.
cases.script:
cu() { if [[ $(type -t coreutils) == builtin ]]; then coreutils "$@"; else "$@"; fi; }; umask 077
before=$(umask)
cu mknod -m 0640 existing p
rc=0; cu mknod -m 0666 existing p || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
rc=0; cu mknod -m 0666 absent/pipe p || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 && $(umask) == "$before" ]]
: > after
printf "preserved\n"
